counterexampleDispositions.1: Covered. A1 is the sole admission event and A4 urgent invalidation closes A1 immediately; an action not consumed before invalidation is denied; the gate owns forwarding through terminal classification.
counterexampleDispositions.10: Covered (strongly). D3 reboot-only maintenance plus secure_mode_policyload locks policy load/booleans/enforcing until reboot; ancestor BPF/SELinux changes require a maintenance-boot reboot that ends the generation (M1/M3).
counterexampleDispositions.11: Covered. W1-W6 preserve original broker parentage via clone3(CLONE_PIDFD|CLONE_INTO_CGROUP) into a pre-frozen delegated leaf; the spec explicitly rejects systemd-child/OCI/subreaper adoption as a substitute.
counterexampleDispositions.12: Covered (design; T06 residual). A2 VAP checks the final post-defaulting object against the signed manifest with an enumerated per-kind defaulted-field allowlist; unexpected effects keep exact-UID cleanup ownership.
counterexampleDispositions.13: Covered. P10 zero-resource uniformity requires the same observer view; 4.1 keeps the gate resident and denying in zero-resource mode so no fake policy or skipped observation.
counterexampleDispositions.14: Covered. G06 v2 record with closed roles and 4.4 mutual v1/v2 rejection; a v2 record that puts the gate under the BROKER key/path or enrolls it as an old role refuses; no permissive parser.
counterexampleDispositions.15: Covered. I04 bytes unchanged; I05 and the new I07 are local AF_UNIX interfaces explicitly enumerated and versioned (not hidden); 6.3 and scope.json confirm no new header/field/credential and no remote-control transport.
counterexampleDispositions.16: Covered. All E01-E12 remain OPEN_UNPROVEN and T01-T08 unexecuted; the candidate repeatedly states it is not native enforcement; this review is read-only source-only.
counterexampleDispositions.17: Covered for transport buffering. C2 flush-on-arm + listen-backlog drain, C3 stamp-at-accept, C5 one-consumption-per-stamp and C7 mutation uniqueness exclude a buffered duplicate of A from consuming a later identical B (6.2). The only residual is an application-level resend (6.3), honestly stated and bounded to at most one B effect with no unarmed effect; it remains a T02/native case.
counterexampleDispositions.18: Covered. A3 drain fence blocks any I07 WRITE_OBJECT (and other writers) while an admitted CREATE lacks a terminal classification; the urgent path records ADMITTED_BEFORE_INVALIDATION (A4). Also listed as 9.18.
counterexampleDispositions.19: Covered. planeon-host-containment.service has RefuseManualStart=yes, sealed unit type, and after S4 planeon_containment_enabled=0 is frozen by secure_mode_policyload so the domain cannot be re-entered until reboot.
counterexampleDispositions.2: Covered. A1 states admission is at pre-forward consumption, not socket accept, TLS, ARM_ACTION ack or worker report; a request parsed under a now-invalid generation cannot pass A1.
counterexampleDispositions.20: Covered. P2 denies name_connect to planeon_kubeapi_port_t from every domain except the enumerated ones, independent of any leftover kubeconfig credential (the confined admin domain is explicitly denied the port).
counterexampleDispositions.21: Covered. C6 and base rule: a gate restart starts deny-first and HELD with no stamps restored, so no connection can be resumed.
counterexampleDispositions.22: Covered. A connection K opened while A is armed is stamped A at accept (C3); after B is armed, C4 refuses K because its stamp != currently armed action, closing it without forwarding.
counterexampleDispositions.23: Covered. I07 WRITE_OBJECT refuses non-policy and every effect kind (2.4); the writer identity never forwards Pod/ConfigMap/Service.
counterexampleDispositions.24: Covered. 2.5 profile rule: the effective RBAC closure contains no ClusterRole with an aggregationRule; the observer refuses otherwise, so the aggregation controller cannot widen a role in-scope.
counterexampleDispositions.25: Covered. Datastore AF_UNIX connectto is allowed only for the apiserver domain and the data directory is writable only by the datastore domain; restore/replace is possible only in reboot maintenance (P1, 2.2).
counterexampleDispositions.26: Covered. P4 disables CSR signing/approving controllers and keeps the CA key off-host during INSPECTING/ACTIVE; even a minted cert cannot reach the port (P2).
counterexampleDispositions.27: Covered (kernel-verified). v2 removes BPF_PROG_GET_FD_BY_ID (cmd 13, which the source confirms needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN) and uses BPF_OBJ_GET (cmd 7, no capability check) on sealed bpffs pins; readers hold only CAP_NET_ADMIN and CAP_BPF.
counterexampleDispositions.28: Covered (reword per F2). MULTI attachment means legacy prog-less detach fails (source-confirmed: MULTI detach needs a valid prog/link fd), and SELinux denies prog_run on containment-owned programs and labels the cgroup dirs. The 'cannot get an O_PATH fd via dir-search denial' framing is imprecise because cgroup2 supports open_by_handle_at, but the SELinux open/label denial (plus denying the confined admin CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH) still blocks the detach, so the outcome holds.
counterexampleDispositions.3: Covered (design; native residual E10). P3 uses Node+RBAC from sealed config with no authorization webhook and no anonymous/static-token path; 2.3 has the observer re-verify complete effective RBAC each observation; admission is re-evaluated at A1/A2.
counterexampleDispositions.4: Partially covered. External system:masters/impersonate/escalate/bind are excluded by the 2.3 closure, P3/P4 (no such on-disk credential, CA key absent) and P7 (no aggregation/APIService); 2.5 excludes aggregated ClusterRoles. Remaining: the in-apiserver loopback system:masters identity and rbac-bootstrap reconciler are not enumerated (F1) but are sealed-TCB and unreachable from unlisted domains by P2, so not an external bypass; enumerate in W02.
counterexampleDispositions.5: Covered. A1/A2/A3 give explicit admitted-vs-committed semantics and 3.3 disclaims any end-to-end atomic transaction; the drain fence rests on the gate being the sole writer path (G04).
counterexampleDispositions.6: Covered. C7 uses signed never-reused CREATE names; IO_AMBIGUOUS/ADMITTED_BEFORE_INVALIDATION retain the name and ownership; M3 new boot/generation never reuses a prior generation or nonce; no name adoption.
counterexampleDispositions.7: Covered. Base separate-journal fsync-domain rule plus HELD-on-uncertainty is retained; consumed-action tombstones (C6) persist; no automatic redispatch.
counterexampleDispositions.8: Covered. Gate/broker/server disagreement on UID or result classification surfaces in the existing RESOURCE_RESULT agreement check (6.3) and becomes HELD; records retained.
counterexampleDispositions.9: Covered. BIND_EXECUTION binds the broker peer qualification digest and generation; peer death is an A4 invalidation that closes A1; no reconnect; W6 waitid/pidfd lifetime enforcement.

findings.finding: 2.3 states 'Only these identities can reach the apiserver' but omits the apiserver's own in-process loopback client, which Kubernetes creates at startup with a random bearer token in group system:masters (verified in apiserver config.go AuthorizeClientBearerToken), and the rbac/bootstrap-roles PostStartHook that reconciles ClusterRoles/ClusterRoleBindings on every start as that identity (verified in storage_rbac.go). These are policy-kind writers not listed in the 2.3 closure or the 2.5 autonomous-writer table. They are inside the sealed-apiserver TCB and unreachable from unlisted domains by P2, so they are not an external bypass, but the closure claim is literally incomplete.
findings.requiredChange: In W02, enumerate the apiserver loopback system:masters identity and the rbac/bootstrap-roles reconciler explicitly (as sealed-TCB, bootstrap-config-pinned, re-verified by the observer's effective-RBAC check each observation), so 2.3's 'only these identities' statement is exact.

findings.finding: 5.1 argues that denying 'dir search' on labelled planeon cgroup directories means 'no other domain can even get an O_PATH fd'. cgroup2 is mounted on kernfs with KERNFS_ROOT_SUPPORT_EXPORTOP (verified in cgroup.c), so a directory fd can also be obtained via open_by_handle_at, and with CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH that path bypasses DAC search checks (verified in fs/fhandle.c may_decode_fh). The effective defense is the SELinux label check at open (and the confined-admin domain lacking CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH), not the 'cannot get an fd' framing.
findings.requiredChange: Reword 5.1/counterexample 28 so the stated mechanism is the SELinux open/label denial on planeon cgroup types (which applies regardless of how the dentry is resolved, including via file handles) plus denial of CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH to the confined admin domain, rather than relying on inability to obtain an O_PATH fd. Outcome is unchanged; the argument should cite the actual gate.

findings.finding: v2 relocates role cgroups from the v1 record's fixed /sys/fs/cgroup/planeon-live/{...} to /sys/fs/cgroup/planeon.slice/planeon-*.service, which is a deliberate versioned change consistent with G06 and the F01 feasibility concern (hand-created planeon-live paths were not a supported systemd delegation plan). This is correct but the path change is a substantive v2 record delta that W02 must carry with explicit old/new rejection vectors; it is flagged so it is not mistaken for an unchanged detail.
findings.requiredChange: No change required for this candidate; W02 must specify the exact v2 cgroup paths and ensure a v1 reader rejects the v2 path layout and vice versa (already asserted in 4.4).

G04.reason: Concrete backend SEALED_SINGLE_NODE_CONTROL_PLANE_V1 with P1-P10, API-path closure (2.2), identity/permission closure (2.3), I07 sole writer (2.4), autonomous-writer table (2.5) and writer-family map (2.6). Host-only properties are named residual native evidence (E03,E04,E05,E10 in 8). No Kubernetes distribution selected and no native enforcement claimed. Residual gap (see F1) is the apiserver's in-process loopback system:masters identity plus the rbac/bootstrap-roles PostStartHook reconciler, which are not enumerated in 2.3/2.5; they sit inside the sealed-apiserver TCB and are unreachable from unlisted domains by P2, so they do not open an external bypass, but W02 should list them. Meets the RESOLVED_DESIGN bar.

G05.reason: POLICY-ADMISSION-SEMANTICS/v2 names A1 (pre-forward gate linearization), A2 (in-apiserver ValidatingAdmissionPolicy pre-persist, stable since v1.30 and running after mutating admission), A3 (drain fence) and A4 (explicitly weaker, recorded). 3.3 disclaims any end-to-end transaction. Accepted bytes of POLICY_OBSERVATION_READINESS.md are unchanged (verified by git diff). A4 is honestly presented as weaker, not equivalent. Residuals A2 field allowlists (T06) named.

G06.reason: Record planeon.internal.native-qualification/v2 with closed resident roles (SERVER/OBSERVER/BROKER/WORKER/EFFECT_GATE), closed lifecycle subjects (HOST_CONTAINMENT/POLICY_WRITER), closed backendComponents, and v1/v2 mutual rejection with no fallback (4.4). No new root key or signing role (reuses pinned root pubkey, 4.2). Gate always resident and denying so the parser has no mode-dependent branch. No reinterpretation or nonce/generation reuse of v1 data. Residual E07 named.

G07.reason: 5.1 kernel findings independently verified against Linux v6.12; boot/seal S1-S6; per-role capability/seccomp/SELinux table (5.3) with no blanket CAP_SYS_ADMIN and no CAP_SYS_PTRACE/CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE anywhere; worker original-parent lifecycle W1-W6; reboot-only maintenance M1-M5. Each row is a design selection; completeness on a real host and the kernel/policy facts are named residual T04/E01-E08 evidence (8). The capability split is internally consistent for same-uid /proc peer inspection (broker inspects the frozen child before its W4 uid change; workers read only world-readable parent stat). Per-arch syscall allowlists deferred to W02 as data.

G09.reason: Connection stamping C1-C7 on unchanged I04: C2 flush-on-arm (closes unconsumed accepted connections and drains the listen backlog), C3 stamp-at-accept (gate state, not client-supplied), C4/C5 one consumption per stamp, C7 mutation uniqueness by construction. This is the transport restriction the base brief required; no new header/field/caller actionId (6.3; scope.json newHeaderOrFieldIntroduced=false). The sole residual (6.3 application-level resend) is stated, bounded to at most one B effect with no unarmed effect, and routed to the existing RESOURCE_RESULT agreement check (HELD). scope.json honestly marks requestActionCorrelationProven=false (behaviour under load/restart is T02/T03). Meets the bar.

questionAnswers.Q1: Yes. C2+C3 exclude counterexample 17 for every place a transport duplicate can be buffered. A buffered duplicate must sit on a connection that already exists at ARM(B): if accepted it has either consumed its one action (C1 one-request-per-connection, so it is finished per C5) or not consumed one, in which case C2 closes it without forwarding; if still in the kernel accept/listen backlog, C2 explicitly accepts and closes it; a connection whose TLS handshake completes after ARM(B) is accepted afterwards and stamped by C3 with the then-armed action, so it cannot carry a stale pre-ARM duplicate without the application itself resending (the 6.3 residual, not transport). Gate-parser-queued bytes belong to an accepted-but-unconsumed connection and are flushed by C2. The exclusion holds for the kernel accept queue, in-connection TLS records, parser queues and post-ARM handshakes.
questionAnswers.Q2: Yes. The 6.3 residual (application resend identical to B while B is armed) is correctly bounded: the forwarded bytes equal B's armed request-template digest (C4), so no unarmed effect can occur; B is consumed once and all other B-stamped connections are closed (C5) with mutation uniqueness by construction (C7), so at most one B effect occurs; a misattributed stale-A-as-B shows up as gate/server disagreement in the existing RESOURCE_RESULT agreement check and becomes HELD. The residual requires the trusted server's own behaviour, is disclosed rather than hidden, and is routed to T02/native, matching the base threat model.
questionAnswers.Q3: The v6.12 claims in 5.1/5.4 all match the fetched torvalds/linux v6.12 source. Confirmed: bpf_prog_get_fd_by_id requires capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN); bpf_prog_query requires bpf_net_capable() (CAP_NET_ADMIN or CAP_SYS_ADMIN); bpf_prog_get_info_by_fd zeroes xlated_prog_len without bpf_capable() and withholds blinded instructions / zeroes helper-call immediates unless bpf_dump_raw_ok==kallsyms_show_value (kptr_restrict + CAP_SYSLOG); BPF_OBJ_GET (cmd 7) has no capability check in bpf_obj_get/bpf_obj_get_user (path_permission plus security_bpf_prog PROG_RUN only); bpf_jit_harden 0 or 1 with CAP_BPF leaves programs unblinded; cgroup attach/detach (bpf_prog_attach/detach, cgroup_bpf_prog_attach/detach) check no capability; legacy non-MULTI detach via find_detach_entry accepts prog==NULL while MULTI detach requires a valid prog/link fd; cgroup_v1v2_get_from_fd uses fdget_raw (O_PATH accepted); selinux_bpf checks only MAP_CREATE and PROG_LOAD at cmd dispatch; unprivileged_bpf_disabled gates only map_create and bpf_prog_load. The 5.4 freeze claim is confirmed: cgroup_post_fork sets JOBCTL_TRAP_FREEZE on a non-kthread child of a CGRP_FREEZE cgroup and calculate_sigpending/recalc_sigpending force the freezer trap before return to user space. UAPI command/attach-type/prog-type numbers match. One-way sysctls (modules_disabled, kexec_load_disabled transition-to-1-only; yama ptrace_scope max-lock) confirmed. VAP stable@v1.30 and 'mutating before validating' confirmed in Kubernetes docs.
questionAnswers.Q4: Yes. A2 (in-apiserver ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, failurePolicy Fail, after mutating admission and before persistence) is a sound pre-persist position for the actual post-mutation manifest: Kubernetes runs mutating admission first (confirmed), so A2 sees the post-defaulting object, and VAP is in-process so it needs no external webhook (P6 keeps webhooks absent). Allowed differences are an enumerated per-kind defaulted-field allowlist fixed in W02 (residual T06). A4 is honestly weaker: it is labelled 'explicitly weaker, recorded', records ADMITTED_BEFORE_INVALIDATION, never relabels the action unadmitted, and 3.3 disclaims equivalence to the original strict wording.
questionAnswers.Q5: Largely yes. Given P2 (loopback-only labelled port with name_connect limited to gate/observer/enumerated control-plane components), P8 (closed in-cluster clients, no Pod SA tokens) and P9 (runtime socket kubelet-only), 2.3 covers the externally reachable identities (gate effect, gate writer, observer, kubelet, per-controller controller-manager, scheduler, service-proxy/network-policy agent). The one omission is the apiserver's own loopback system:masters client and the rbac bootstrap reconciler (finding F1); these are sealed-TCB and not an external bypass but should be enumerated. The 2.5 autonomous-writer table is plausible as a starting inventory (aggregation, SA/token, namespace-lifecycle, ResourceQuota status, root-CA publisher, CSR, GC/EndpointSlice) with distribution-specific additions explicitly deferred to W02.
questionAnswers.Q6: Acceptable. systemd documents that delegation is available on service/scope units and expressly NOT on slice units (verified in the pinned CGROUP_DELEGATION.md). v2's refinement puts one service per role under planeon.slice and gives Delegate=yes only to planeon-capacity-broker.service, which exclusively owns the broker and probe-worker leaves; the slice itself is not delegated. Raw cgroup ownership therefore remains a single delegated service, satisfying the spirit of MET-ENFORCE-001 decision 2 while the non-delegated roles are ordinary systemd-managed services (single-writer owned by systemd, read-only inspectable). This also resolves the v1 F01 concern that hand-created /sys/fs/cgroup/planeon-live paths were not a supported delegation plan. It does not need to collapse to a single service because only the broker requires raw cgroup access. The reviewer confirms this is the explicit refinement the brief asked to check.
questionAnswers.Q7: The 8 residual-native list is essentially complete: it names 2-closure completeness (E03-E05,E10), 5.1 kernel facts on the enrolled kernel/policy and the secure_mode_policyload conditionals in the pinned binary policy (T04), freeze-before-user-space under CLONE_INTO_CGROUP (T04/T05), C2/C3 flush/stamp under load and restart (T02/T03), and A2 field allowlists (T06). The one item that should be added for completeness is the apiserver loopback system:masters identity / rbac-bootstrap reconciler (finding F1), which is implicitly within the E10/2-closure residual but not spelled out. No RESOLVED_DESIGN claim rests on an undisclosed native assumption beyond that; the kernel-level assumptions this review could check against source all held.

reviewLimit: Read-only source-only design review of the exact hashed subject files against the listed predecessor inputs and independently fetched Linux v6.12 and Kubernetes/systemd upstream source. It establishes only that the five gates meet the RESOLVED_DESIGN bar at design level and that the cited kernel/Kubernetes facts match upstream source. It is NOT W01 native completion, coding readiness, an adopted wire ABI, an installed gate, native enforcement, selection of a Kubernetes distribution, closure of any E01-E12 obligation, nor tenant/native acceptance. No host was observed; kernel facts were read from source, not run; all behaviour under load, restart and on the enrolled kernel/policy remains unproven (T01-T08, E01-E12 OPEN_UNPROVEN).
